title: Orbit-simulated-mini-canary-with-weighted-synthetic-smoke-and-autorepair
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: enable a lightweight, reproducible mini-canary that uses a small synthetic traffic generator informed by orbit simulator traces to calibrate A/B and canary weight ramps without impacting production traffic. This change introduces: 1) a weighted synthetic-smoke generator that produces controllable request distributions (user-agent, payload size, session-stickiness) derived from sampled orbit traces; 2) a rendezvous runner that schedules mini-canaries in a sandboxed slice with automatic health probes and rollback triggers; 3) an autorepair handler that attempts graceful remediation (restart, warmup-snapshots, degrade-to-shadow) before triggering full rollback; 4) console controls and runbook docs for operators to start/stop and visualize synthetic smoke; 5) e2e fixtures and CI gating to reduce flaky failures. Security/privacy: synthetic traces are aggregated and anonymized; no customer PII is used. Rollout plan: gated rollout to staging for 48h, opt-in on Dedicated clusters, monitor canary_metrics and latency/accuracy deltas, then gradual rollout to production lanes. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration e2e harness, [x] docs + runbook, [x] alerting hooks, [x] Linear links. Impact: reduces risk for model promotes by allowing pre-promote calibration and automated self-heal attempts, lowers manual triage for transient infra noise. Related: ENG-2314 for orbit sampling, PM-989 for canary UX improvements.
